symptom: `create workflow … display 'Approval for {1} by {2}' with ({1} = $WorkflowContext/Title, …)` failed with "extraneous input 'WITH' expecting one of {ON, BEGIN, …}" and a misleading hint about `/`; a user task's task name was always its caption, so the inbox text Studio Pro shows could not be set, and a describe -> create or modify reset a Studio Pro task name and its parameters (the #1713 refusal)
cause: The header's DISPLAY/DESCRIPTION and the user task's DESCRIPTION took a bare STRING_LITERAL; there was no task-name clause; the writer wrote every Microflows$StringTemplate with an empty Parameters list and the reader read only Text
insight: mx check is the oracle that made this cheap without Studio Pro: it PARSES a template parameter's expression, so patching a stored unit and running it settled both the shape (Microflows$TemplateParameter{Expression} under StringTemplate.Parameters — gen calls it TemplateArgument, whose storage name it is; the REST writer's stringTemplateElem already wrote it) and the scope table (display/description: $WorkflowContext only; task name/description: plus $WorkflowInstance; $WorkflowUserTask and $currentUser CE0117), plus CE0720 for an unfilled placeholder and CE0716 for {0}. Contrast mx check accepting a bogus recurrence IntervalType (#1716): an oracle proves only what it validates — run a bogus control first. `name` is an attribute name everywhere, so `task name` is TASK + IDENTIFIER checked in the visitor rather than a NAME keyword. MCP refuses parameters instead of writing the text without them, since PED's list shape for them is unmeasured
fix: `with ({1} = <expr>, …)` after display/description/task name/description in CREATE and in ALTER `set (Display|Description|TaskName: '…' with (…))`; writer emits TemplateParameter children, reader returns them, describe prints them (task name only when it is not the caption); MDL-WF21 refuses unfilled/zero placeholders and gapped numbering, MDL-WF19 checks the parameters' scope; the #1713 rewrite refusal drops its template rows
